earlier_scan.source_named: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. Dialectology as Dialectic: Interpreting Phula Variation. De Gruyter (phonological data on Muji varieties incl. Bokha)
earlier_scan.note: Paywalled monograph; Glottolog lists only Pelkey 2007/2011 wordlist-level data for ybk

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record bokh1237 Bokha (Glottolog's most extensive descriptions: Pelkey 2011 and Pelkey 2007, both 'a wordlist or less'); Wikidata Q63340714; en.wikipedia 'Bokha language' (redirect to 'Muji language', sole source Pelkey 2011)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No descriptive source for Bokha beyond Pelkey's wordlist-level comparative works; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International. 144 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bokha is datapoint YBZ ('Bokha: Pingbian County, Dishuiceng, Yibaizu') in the datapoint list, clade table and one cognate remark in sec. 4.6 (Muji meso-clade); the phonology-in-brief sections cover Phola, Phuza, Southern Muji, Hlepho Phowa and Azha only; the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the book. SILENT.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority / Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Change Request 2007-094 and Request for New Language Code Element [ybk] Bokha (adopted 2008-01-14). SIL International. 8 + 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: identity, names (Bokha, Bokho, Hei Muji, Hua Phula, Aphu, Akapa, Lao Phula, Pao Tle), location, RTT intelligibility scores and sources only; the sole linguistic source cited is Pelkey's forthcoming 2008 La Trobe PhD.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Muji's mirrored merger: correlative redistribution of checked tone classes in a newly defined Burmic cluster. Mon-Khmer Studies 37: 179-195.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bokha = datapoint 'Yibaizu village, Dishuiceng district, Pingbian county' in the checked-tone-class correspondence tables; the 'sample phonology sketch' (sec. 2, pp. 181-183) is of Muji-PJZ (Southern Muji) only; no mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere. SILENT.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2005. Puzzling over Phula: Toward the synthesis and statement of a Tibeto-Burman language cluster. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 28(2): 43-78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Literature survey of Chinese sources on Phula; 'Bokha' does not occur; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 2003. Three Tibeto-Burman languages of Vietnam. In David Bradley, Randy LaPolla, Boyd Michailovsky & Graham Thurgood (eds.), Language variation: papers on variation and change in the Sinosphere and in the Indosphere in honour of James A. Matisoff, 305-320. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 555.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Cited in the ISO change request for the former Vietnamese Bokha villages; describes Phula varieties of Vietnam (not Bokha proper) and would at most give an out-group comparison; low priority and identity uncertain.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. Dialectology as Dialectic: Interpreting Phula Variation. Trends in Linguistics 229. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. xxxiv+498 pp. (ch. 5 pp. 223-270 five phonological sketches; ch. 6 pp. 271-351 Muji-clade tone correspondences with Bokha-YBZ data)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL3311.Y5 P45 2011) (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL3311.Y5 P45 2011
sources.note: The only published work with primary Bokha phonological data (tone-class reflexes, segmental notes such as nasal-coda reintroduction in the YBZ dialect); a full read is needed to confirm the snippet-index finding that it contains no word-stress statement for Bokha or for any Phula lect.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2008. The Phula languages in synchronic and diachronic perspective. PhD thesis, La Trobe University, Melbourne. 439 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists at the publisher (DOI recorded); open or paywalled, not checked
sources.note: Source of all Bokha data (2005-06 survey of Bokha-YBZ and Bokho-DXB); may contain more of the raw wordlist/tone data than the 2011 revision; the only other candidate for any prosodic remark on Bokha.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2005-2006. Phula survey wordlists and RTT recordings, Bokha-YBZ (Yibaizu, Dishuiceng, Pingbian) and Bokho-DXB (Dixibei). SIL International East Asia Group, unpublished field data.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only primary Bokha corpus in existence; a recording-based check of word-level prominence would have to start here.
